_comment: Declarative source adapters. To add a projection source, drop the .xlsx in sources/
and add an entry here -- no Python changes needed.
columns / goalie_columns values may be either:
a string  -> matched against the header row text (case/space insensitive)
an integer-> 1-based column index (use when headers repeat, e.g. Yahoo has two 'GP')
Stat keys not present in a source are simply omitted; the blender skips that source
for those stats rather than treating them as zero.
Goalies: leave them on the main sheet and use 'goalie_columns' to remap only the
columns that differ (Yahoo), or set 'goalie_sheet' when they live on a sheet of
their own with a different layout (DtZ). With 'goalie_sheet', 'goalie_columns' is
the full mapping for that sheet.
rate_stats are averaged directly and never rescaled by games played -- multiplying
a save percentage by GP would be meaningless.
_adp_comment: ADP is not one number. Yahoo's board and Fantrax's disagree by 47.8 picks
on average and by as much as 164, so which one you read genuinely changes
'mean_of' computes a provider from others: the mean of whichever of them
rank a player. That rule was verified against a published average column
Sources that publish a single unlabelled ADP are assigned to the platform
they track: DtZ's matches Fantrax (0% exact against Yahoo), Daily Faceoff's
matches Yahoo (45% exact, 0% against Fantrax). They are read as gap-fillers
-- the first source listed wins wherever it has a value, so a provider is
one board topped up from a second snapshot, not two blended together.
'values' maps provider id -> column. 'value' (a bare column) still works and
_eligibility_comment: Position eligibility is a platform ruling, not a projection. None of the
sources can supply it -- all five ship one position string and agree on 683
of the 687 players that more than one of them carries -- so each platform's
list is an optional file in config/.
These lists were extracted from a pair of workbooks published against each
platform, which differ on the POS column for 133 players. Regenerate with
'python make_eligibility.py' if you have those files; the rulings are
Yahoo's and Fantrax's own, not any projection source's work.
Drop a file in and that platform appears in the board's settings menu.
Leave it out and it does not. Format: 'name,positions', positions separated
_source_order_comment: Order matters for identity only: the first source carrying a player supplies
the display name, team and position, and later sources fill blanks. Most
complete first, so one source names nearly everyone rather than the board
taking spellings from whoever happens to be listed earliest. It has no
effect on the blend, where every source is weighted the same way.

_note: A plain CSV export. Two columns are headed PTS -- column 6 is fantasy
points under their own scoring and column 8 is goals + assists -- so
they are addressed by index and only the second is mapped.
Goalies in this file leave GP blank and record games in GS (24), which
is what goalie_columns is for. Teams are nicknames ('Avalanche'), which
teams.normalize resolves, and missing values are em dashes.

_schedule_comment: Team schedule strength, from the @HockeyBangers 2026-27 schedule pack.
Two things that change a player's real value and appear in no projection:
how many games fall on off-nights (you can only start so many skaters, so
games on light nights actually get used) and how many games land in the
The playoffs sheet holds TWO tables. Skipping the final week shifts the
whole three-round window a week earlier -- it is NOT the first table minus
its last column -- so both are read by row range and never derived from
each other. 'skip' is the default and matches most Yahoo leagues.
Indicator only: none of this touches the blend or VORP.
_history_comment: Last season's ACTUAL results, not a projection. Deliberately outside
'sources' so it can never enter the weighted blend -- it is scored with your
settings and ranked separately, purely for comparison.
These files are HTML tables saved with a .xls extension (format: html).
Row 1 is a group banner, so header_row is 2.
Traded players appear once per team plus a '2TM' aggregate row; dedupe_by
with prefer_team_suffix keeps only the aggregate.
Hockey-Reference splits power-play GOALS (col 13) from power-play ASSISTS
(col 17), so PPP has to be derived as their sum; likewise SHP from 14 + 18.
